es: Decidir si un comentario es sincero o sarcástico a partir del contexto, el contraste y las pistas de tono escritas.

teaching.en: When Leo says “Thanks a lot” in a flat voice after Ana spills coffee on his notes, he is sarcastic.
teaching.es: Cuando Leo dice «Muchas gracias» con voz plana después de que Ana derrama café sobre sus apuntes, está siendo sarcástico.
teaching.explanationEs: Una voz plana con un contexto negativo es una pista de sarcasmo.
segments: When Leo says “Thanks a lot” in a flat voice
after Ana spills coffee on his notes, he is sarcastic.
teaching.audioText: When Leo says “Thanks a lot” in a flat voice after Ana spills coffee on his notes, he is sarcastic.

teaching.en: “You are so helpful,” said Mia with a long sigh, and the cue told everyone that the praise was not sincere.
teaching.es: «Eres tan servicial», dijo Mia con un largo suspiro, y la pista dejó claro a todos que el elogio no era sincero.
teaching.explanationEs: El suspiro es una pista: el elogio suena falso.
segments: “You are so helpful,” said Mia with a long sigh, and
the cue told everyone that the praise was not sincere.
teaching.audioText: “You are so helpful,” said Mia with a long sigh, and the cue told everyone that the praise was not sincere.

teaching.en: There is often a contrast between happy words and a tired face, and that contrast clearly marks sarcasm.
teaching.es: A menudo hay un contraste entre palabras alegres y una cara cansada, y ese contraste marca claramente el sarcasmo.
teaching.explanationEs: El contraste entre palabras y gesto delata el sarcasmo.
segments: There is often a contrast between happy words and
a tired face, and that contrast clearly marks sarcasm.
teaching.audioText: There is often a contrast between happy words and a tired face, and that contrast clearly marks sarcasm.

teaching.en: It was such a long meeting that Tom let out a sigh of relief when it ended.
teaching.es: Fue una reunión tan larga que Tom soltó un suspiro de alivio cuando terminó.
teaching.explanationEs: Such a + adjetivo + nombre intensifica; después, that introduce el resultado.
segments: It was such a long meeting that Tom let
out a sigh of relief when it ended.
teaching.audioText: It was such a long meeting that Tom let out a sigh of relief when it ended.

teaching.en: “Your cooking is surprisingly good” is a backhanded compliment, and its sarcastic edge is thinly disguised.
teaching.es: «Tu cocina es sorprendentemente buena» es un cumplido con doble filo, y su punta sarcástica apenas está disimulada.
teaching.explanationEs: Un elogio que esconde una crítica: «surprisingly» revela que esperaba lo contrario.
segments: “Your cooking is surprisingly good” is a backhanded
compliment, and its sarcastic edge is thinly disguised.

teaching.en: A flat voice can give the game away even when the words are polite, so always listen for the cue.
teaching.es: Una voz plana puede delatar la intención aunque las palabras sean corteses, así que escucha siempre la pista.
teaching.explanationEs: Give the game away: dejar al descubierto lo que alguien quería ocultar.

prompt.es: Lee la escena: ¿qué pista delata que Carlos no es sincero?

choices.text: The schedule was new, so he is confused.
His flat voice and sigh contradict his words.
His words are positive, so they are sincere.

feedback.es: Carlos dice que todo está claro, pero el suspiro y la voz plana van en sentido contrario: el tono delata el sarcasmo.

hint.es: Mira qué hacen su voz y su cuerpo mientras habla.

origin.text: After Sara had explained the new schedule for the third time, Carlos sighed, looked at the ceiling and said in a flat voice, “Oh, that is so clear now.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue un viaje tan largo que todos nos dormimos.»

feedback.es: Con un nombre (journey) detrás del adjetivo se usa such a; so solo acompañaría a un adjetivo suelto.

hint.es: Después del espacio vienen a + adjetivo + nombre.

origin.text: The train was delayed twice, and then it stopped for an hour in an empty field. It was ___ a long journey that we all fell asleep.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada pista con lo que revela sobre el comentario.

pairs.es: cansancio o fastidio tras las palabras

pairs: a contrast between words and facts

pairs.es: lo dicho choca con la situación

feedback.es: Las cuatro son pistas de sarcasmo: dos de tono, una de contexto y una de contenido.

hint.es: Piensa si la pista está en la voz, en el gesto o en la situación.

pairs.es: cansancio o fastidio tras las palabras

pairs: a contrast between words and facts

prompt.es: Escucha la escena: ¿qué quiere decir Mia con «you are so reliable»?

choices.text: That Leo has done well and deserves thanks.
That Leo is reliable, although he forgot one thing.
That Leo is not reliable, and she is annoyed.

feedback.es: El suspiro y las manos vacías contradicen el elogio: Mia usa «reliable» con sarcasmo para reprochar el olvido.

origin.audio: Leo had promised to bring the tickets for the concert, but he arrived at the station with empty hands. Mia looked at him, gave a long sigh and said, “Well, you are so reliable.” Everybody laughed except Leo, who stared at the floor.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento: ¿qué hace sarcástico el segundo comentario de Sara?

choices.text: She repeats the word plan in both remarks.
She speaks while she is busy with her phone.
She uses a longer sentence than in her first remark.
The praise comes just after she finds the Sunday meetings.

feedback.es: El contexto decide: felicita a Carlos justo cuando descubre reuniones en domingo, así que el elogio es una crítica disfrazada.

origin.text: Carlos handed Sara the new schedule. “It is such a lovely plan,” said Sara, without looking up from her phone. Then she put the phone down, turned the page, found the same meetings on Sunday, and added, “Really, you have thought of everything.”

prompt.es: Ordena: «Fue una reunión tan larga que todos suspiraron.»

answer.text: It was such a long meeting that everybody sighed

feedback.es: Such a + adjetivo + nombre va seguido de that + resultado: la estructura intensifica y explica la consecuencia.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato: ¿cómo responde la jefa al comentario de Carlos?

choices.text: She has understood the sarcasm and answers it with a polite challenge.
She takes his remark as a genuine compliment and rewards him with a new task.
She feels hurt by his comment and brings the meeting to an end at once.
She accepts that the rota needs more work and thanks him for his honesty.

feedback.es: Sonríe y le pide que organice el siguiente: es un desafío cortés que muestra que captó el sarcasmo, y Carlos lo entiende así.

origin.audio: Our manager presented the new weekend rota for the third time, and each time it had changed. When she finished, my colleague Carlos put his hand up and said, in a perfectly flat voice, that he had rarely seen such a well organised plan. Nobody spoke. The manager smiled, thanked him warmly and asked whether he would like to help organise the next one. Carlos went pale and said that, on reflection, the plan was not so bad. Afterwards Sara whispered that she respected his courage, because sarcasm is always a risk when the listener is also the boss.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la postura de quien escribe sobre el sarcasmo con su hijo adolescente?

choices.text: It is dangerous, so she should never use it with young people.
It is acceptable when the son can answer back in the same way.
It is better than a lecture in every family conversation she has.
It is a habit that she has copied from her own sixteen-year-old son.

feedback.es: No lo rechaza ni lo defiende sin más: lo acepta mientras el hijo pueda responder igual, porque solo duele cuando no hay réplica.

origin.text: I am told that I should not use sarcasm with my sixteen-year-old son. Perhaps so. But when he says that cleaning his room is a lovely chance, he is hardly sincere himself, and I find a dry reply more honest than a lecture. Sarcasm only hurts when the listener has no chance to answer in kind.

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue un cumplido envenenado, cortés por fuera e hiriente por dentro.»

feedback.es: Backhanded compliment es la colocación para un elogio que contiene una crítica: amable en apariencia, hiriente en el fondo.

origin.text: When Sara won the prize, her opponent said, “Congratulations, you must be surprised that the judges chose you.” It was a ___ compliment, polite on the surface and rude inside.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada comentario con la lectura correcta según su situación.

pairs: “What a lovely surprise!” to a friend who brings flowers

pairs.es: sincero: la situación justifica el elogio

pairs: “What a lovely surprise!” said flatly to a neighbour who plays loud music at midnight

pairs.es: sarcástico: la situación contradice la frase

pairs: “Thanks a lot” said with a sigh when a colleague leaves you all the work

pairs.es: sarcástico: el suspiro delata el reproche

pairs: “Thanks a lot” said warmly when a colleague covers your shift

pairs.es: sincero: el agradecimiento encaja con el gesto

feedback.es: La misma frase cambia de sentido según el contexto y el gesto: cada pareja lo demuestra con una versión sincera y una sarcástica.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la abuela con su comentario sobre el traje?

choices.text: That she respects his courage in choosing the colour.
That he will be easy to find if he gets lost.
That the suit is too loud, though she avoids saying so.
That she would prefer him to buy a different suit.

feedback.es: La abuela nunca critica de frente: «nobody will lose you» es un cumplido con doble filo, y el resto de la familia capta el tono.

origin.text: My grandmother never says anything rude. When my cousin arrived in a bright orange suit, she looked him up and down and said, “Well, nobody will lose you in a crowd.” He took it as a compliment. The rest of the family, who know her tone, did not.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nadie le creyó, porque su voz plana lo delató.»

answer.text: Nobody believed him because his flat voice gave the game away

feedback.es: Give the game away lleva el objeto en medio: gave the game away, con la causa introducida por because.

prompt.es: Escucha la anécdota: ¿por qué entiende el camarero la queja al instante?

choices.text: Because the uncle had complained about the same soup several times before.
Because the uncle asked him openly to change the soup.
Because the waiter had already noticed that the soup was cold.
Because what the uncle said clashed with what was plainly on the table.

feedback.es: Elogiar una «warm welcome» ante un plato frío es un contraste evidente: el camarero capta la queja sin que se formule.

origin.audio: When the waiter asked how the soup was, my uncle looked at the cold bowl, sighed and said that it was such a warm welcome. The waiter understood at once and offered to heat it up, because the contrast between the words and the bowl was painfully clear.
